extracted.intended_audience: museums and eligible organizations applying for IMLS Museums for America grants (applicants preparing SF-424S, IMLS Budget Form, Program Information Form, and Digital Products Plan)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application (forms, budget, justifications, registrations, and digital products plan) for the IMLS Museums for America grant program, ensuring compliance with program-specific procedural, budgetary, and stewardship requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal Welfare Act certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant certifies that the project will comply with the Animal Welfare Act of 1966, as amended (7 U.S.C. § 2131 et seq.) pertaining to the care, handling, and treatment of warm-blooded animals held for research, teaching, or other activities supported by this award of assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact IMLS for further information on these certifications. Include this certification where applicable in the application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) has replaced the D-U-N-S® Number and is requested in, and assigned by, the System for Award Management (SAM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with active SAM registrations can find their assigned UEI in their SAM records; applicants without active SAM registrations receive a UEI when they register in SAM. See gsa.gov/entityid for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAM registration and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be registered with SAM before registering with Grants.gov and must maintain an active SAM registration with current information at all times while they have an active award or an application under consideration by IMLS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin SAM registration via Login.gov. Allow several weeks for SAM registration. Renew registrations at least every 12 months and sooner if information changes. An expired or incomplete SAM registration can prevent submission and award; IMLS may not make an award until all UEI and SAM requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov registration and AOR roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must register with Grants.gov before submitting an application. After an organization registers and creates an Organizational Applicant Profile, the request for Grants.gov roles is sent to the EBiz POC who assigns roles including the Authorized Organization Representative (AOR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure SAM registration is current before registering. Designate more than one AOR to avoid last-minute crises and update contact information and passwords whenever an AOR changes. Grants.gov Applicant Support contact info is provided for technical assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Grants.gov Workspace
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov applicants apply online using Workspace, a shared online environment where members of a grant team may simultaneously access and edit different forms within an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create individual copies of a workspace for each funding opportunity. Consult Grants.gov Workspace overview resources (graphics, videos, Help Articles) as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424S: Legal applicant information must match SAM
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter your organization’s legal name and address exactly as they appear in your SAM registration. This is the organization with authority to apply directly for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an organizational unit will carry out the project, specify it appropriately on the IMLS Museum Program Information Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424S: Applicant identifiers and codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide web address, type of applicant code, Employer/Taxpayer Identification Number (EIN/TIN), Organizational UEI, and congressional district in specified formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the indicated dropdowns and formats (e.g., congressional district as 'CA-005' or '001' for at-large). For missing UEI contact Federal Service Desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project title and description format
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Title: Enter a brief descriptive title using no more than 200 characters. Project Description: Enter a brief description (about 120 words) describing purpose, activities, deliverables, expected outcomes, and intended beneficiaries in clear language understandable to non-experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS may use the title for public information. Use concise, non-technical language for the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project period date format and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter project start and end dates in mm/dd/yyyy format. The project period begins on the first day of the start month and ends on the last day of the end month. Refer to Section B for allowable start dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure dates align with the period of performance and budget Year 1/2/3 columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique email addresses for key roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Email addresses entered for the Project Director, Primary Contact/Grants Administrator, and Authorized Representatives must be unique to those individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email addresses used by more than one person within an organization are not acceptable to avoid authentication and responsibility conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Director and Authorized Representative distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Director is the person with primary responsibility for carrying out project activities. The Authorized Representative is the person who has authority to legally bind the organization. IMLS requires the Project Director be a different person than the Authorized Representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete Items 7–9 appropriately. The AOR cannot be the same person as the Project Director. The AOR's 'I Agree' certifies compliance with IMLS Assurances and Certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Contact / Grants Administrator role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Primary Contact/Grants Administrator has core responsibility for administering the award and may be the same person as the Project Director in some organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this person is the same as the Project Director, check the box and skip to Item 9. Still complete both Items 8 and 9 if the Primary Contact is the same as the Authorized Representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum Program Information Form: organizational unit and dynamic sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer whether an organizational unit will carry out activities; responses determine subsequent questions dynamically. Provide requested details referencing the entity in Item 5a of the SF-424S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Helpful Definitions on the Program Information Form to determine responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum Program Information Form: financial information (three-year fiscal data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide financial information in the table for the most recently completed fiscal year, the previous year, and the year before that. If an organizational unit was named, ensure the financial information pertains to that unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete figures accurately to reflect organizational financial position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Agency-Level Goal and Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the IMLS agency-level goal and associated objective that best aligns with your proposed project (per Section A1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the best fit to inform reviewer alignment and program reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Program and project category selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Select 'Museums for America' as the Grant Program and then select one project category per Section A2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Section A2 for program goals, objectives, and appropriate categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Element selection to match reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the primary project element that is core to your proposed project to help match your application to reviewers with appropriate experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the element that best reflects the project's central activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum profile and eligibility selections
rubrics_metrics.description: If eligible to apply as a museum, provide selections and information as requested in the Museum Profile (refer to Section C1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure selections reflect organizational status and program eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Request amounts must match budget form
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the amount requested from IMLS and the amount of non-federal cost share/match consistent with the Grant Fund and Cost Share totals in Section 10 of the IMLS Budget Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency between the Program Information Form and the IMLS Budget Form entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs selection per Appendix options
rubrics_metrics.description: Select one option for calculating and including indirect costs in the project budget (options described in Appendix Three).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include using a current federally negotiated rate, a proposed rate pending negotiation, the 10% de minimis MTDC rate if eligible, or excluding indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract content and character limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Write an Abstract of no more than 3,000 characters in concise narrative format for experts and general audiences addressing specified bullets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: lead applicant and collaborators; the need/problem and how identified; high-level activities and timeframe; beneficiaries; intended results; how success will be measured. Paste text into form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Keywords selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Select from one to eight keywords that best characterize the project from options provided on the form (identical list in Appendix Seven).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS may use these keywords in grantmaking compilations and to help others understand supported activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMLS Budget Form: format and multi-year structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Download the IMLS Budget Form (PDF) and work on it outside the browser. The form accommodates up to three years of project activities and expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save as PDF and upload as part of the application. Year 1/2/3 columns correspond to consecutive 12-month periods starting from project start date. Review program-specific timelines and allowable costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable, necessary, auditable, and timely costs
rubrics_metrics.description: All items listed (whether supported by grant funds or cost share) must be necessary to accomplish project objectives, allowable under federal cost principles, auditable, and incurred during the award period of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charges like salaries, fringe, travel, and contractual services must conform to the organization's written policies and practices. Report program income generated with project funds during the award period as program income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget line-item overflow guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If more lines are needed in a specific section of the Budget Form, summarize the information in the IMLS Budget Form and explain further in the Budget Justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively include a separate IMLS Budget Form as a Supporting Document for complex third-party costs and refer to it in the Budget Justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salaries and wages documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include both temporary and permanent staff as well as volunteers engaged in project activities. Document the method of cost computation with base salary or wages and percentage of time allocated to the project (percentage, days, or hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cost share is provided by unpaid volunteers, explain how the dollar value was determined. If requesting IMLS funding for salaries of permanent staff, explain the reason and how regular duties will be covered during the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe benefits can be claimed as a direct cost only for positions included in the direct cost pool and only for the portion of salaries and wages identified for the project. Indicate fringe benefit rate and base to which rate is applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If several persons' fringe benefits were consolidated, break out detail in the Budget Justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel cost computation and airfare rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain method of cost computation for each travel cost, including subsistence, lodging, and transportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the lowest available commercial fares for coach or equivalent accommodations and U.S.-flagged air carriers for foreign travel when such services are available, per applicable U.S. legal requirements. Provide trip-level details in the Budget Justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplies, materials, and equipment listing
rubrics_metrics.description: List costs of supplies, materials, and equipment purchased specifically for the proposed project, including number and unit cost for each item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how amounts were determined in the Budget Justification and provide vendor quotes or price lists as Supporting Documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subawards and contracts listing and designation
rubrics_metrics.description: List each third party (partners, consultants, subgrantees, contractors, collaborators, vendors, service providers) and associated costs as individual line items. Designate each as either a subaward or a contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemize third-party costs in the Budget Justification or include a separate IMLS Budget Form as a Supporting Document. Identify each third party by name, describe role and activities, and explain costs. Determine subaward vs contract per 2 C.F.R. § 200.331. IMLS grant funds generally may not be provided to other U.S. government agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Support costs definition and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Students include those enrolled in community college, undergraduate, graduate, post-master’s or post-doctoral programs focused on career/professional development, and library/archives/museum staff in professional development activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: tuition support, salaries or stipends for graduate assistant work focused on research/teaching, pay/benefits for residents/fellows intended to support learning outcomes, travel/conference registration/support for learning, supplies/equipment for student learning. Use Student Support section for these costs and explain calculation in the Budget Justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities not considered Student Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Students employed in roles that are primarily administrative or clerical, doing work not primarily focused on career/professional development are not Student Support; tuition paid on behalf of these students is not Student Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List such costs in Salaries and Wages rather than Student Support and consult 2 C.F.R. §§ 200.466 and 200.430 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Costs usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the 'Other Costs' section for costs that cannot be assigned to other categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use this section to list items that would fit in lines allotted for another section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Direct Costs entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate total direct costs and specify how much is requested from IMLS and how much is provided as cost share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts will total automatically on the Budget Form; provide clear allocation between grant funds and cost share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs identification
rubrics_metrics.description: If including indirect costs, identify the indirect cost rate (percent) and the base (dollars) to which the rate is applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click provided links for more information about indirect costs; ensure consistency between selected indirect cost option and documentation provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Project Costs entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the total project costs and specify how much is requested from IMLS and how much is provided as cost share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Totals will auto-calculate; ensure accuracy and consistency with other form sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost share rules and ineligible sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost share is the portion of project costs not paid by IMLS and includes cash outlays, property/services contributions, and in-kind contributions (e.g., donated volunteer or consultant time). All expenses, including cost share, must be incurred during the award period unless allowed by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal funds from other federal awards may not be used for cost share. All applicable federal, IMLS, and program requirements apply to both requested IMLS funds and cost share. See 2 C.F.R. §§ 200.1 and 200.306.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for calculating and including indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: You may: (1) use a rate not to exceed your current federally negotiated indirect cost rate (NICRA); (2) use an indirect cost rate proposed to a federal agency for negotiation (if finalized by award); (3) use a rate not to exceed 10% of MTDC if you do not have a NICRA and meet requirements; or (4) not include indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the option that applies and provide required documentation (e.g., current NICRA copy when applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Using a Federally Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate (NICRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your organization has a NICRA in effect, you may use an approved rate in calculating indirect costs; the rate must be applied appropriately and a copy of the current agreement must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may choose a lower rate than in your agreement but not a higher one. Only NICRAs current by the award date will be accepted. The approved rate in the awarded budget applies throughout the life of the award and cannot be changed later even if new rates are negotiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using a proposed indirect cost rate
rubrics_metrics.description: If negotiating a NICRA, you may use the proposed rate to estimate costs, but IMLS will accept it only if negotiations are finalized by the award date and a copy of the final agreement is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS staff will work with you to adjust your budget prior to issuing an award if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10 percent de minimis indirect cost rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for certain State and local government entities described in Appendix VII to 2 C.F.R. part 200, organizations without a current NICRA may choose to charge a de minimis rate of 10 percent of Modified Total Direct Costs (MTDC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the indicated box on the IMLS Budget Form to use this rate; no additional documentation required. MTDC definition and exclusions are provided; consult 2 C.F.R. for more guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Modified Total Direct Costs (MTDC)
rubrics_metrics.description: MTDC means all direct salaries and wages, applicable fringe benefits, materials and supplies, services, travel, and up to the first $25,000 of each subaward. MTDC excludes equipment, capital expenditures, patient care charges, rental costs, tuition remission, scholarships/fellowships, participant support costs, and portions of subawards in excess of $25,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other items may only be excluded when necessary to avoid serious inequity with cognizant agency approval; see 2 C.F.R. § 200.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying an indirect cost rate to cost share
rubrics_metrics.description: You may, consistent with 2 C.F.R. part 200, apply your indirect cost rate to total direct costs covered by cost share, but costs claimed as cost share must be accounted for in the cost share column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS funds can be used for indirect costs only for the portion of total direct costs for which you are requesting IMLS funds (Grant Funds column). See 2 C.F.R. §§ 200.412-414 for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on indirect cost calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a current NICRA, follow its conditions and requirements. If your NICRA is less than 10 percent, you must use it rather than the de minimis rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 2 C.F.R. § 200.414(f) and § 200.1 for further information on restrictions and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification format and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare the Budget Justification following the IMLS Budget Form section headings and save it as a PDF. Address both grant funds and cost share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed narrative and computations for: (1) Salaries and wages (names, roles, base salary, percent time); (2) Fringe benefits (rates and bases); (3) Travel (purpose, origin/destination, traveler name, cost breakdown, computation); (4) Supplies/materials/equipment (number, unit cost, vendor quotes); (5) Subawards/contracts (identify third parties, role, designation as subrecipient or contractor, costs, supporting documents, and the subaward/contract determination per 2 C.F.R. § 200.331); (6) Student Support (calculation method and definition); (7) Other costs; (8) Total Direct Costs (specify IMLS vs cost share); (9) Indirect Costs (identify rate and base); (10) Total Project Costs (specify IMLS vs cost share).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of private nonprofit status
rubrics_metrics.description: Private, nonprofit applicants must submit a copy of the IRS letter indicating eligibility for nonprofit status under the applicable Internal Revenue Code provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS will not accept a state sales tax exemption letter as proof of nonprofit status. See 2 C.F.R. § 3187.7(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan required components
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants proposing to create digital products must prepare and submit a Digital Products Plan describing how they will address Type, Availability, Access, and Sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS staff and peer reviewers will closely scrutinize the plan; organization of the plan to address those four headings is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the digital content, resources, or assets you will create or collect (e.g., still images, audio, moving images, microfilm, object inventories, metadata schema, software, source code), the quantities of each type, the digital file format(s), the accompanying metadata, and any relevant standards you will use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If developing software, specify programming languages, platforms, frameworks, software/tools, and explain reasoning for choices. Use relevant standards and document choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how you will make digital content, resources, assets, software, and metadata available to the public, including delivery strategy (openly available online, available to specified audiences), underlying hardware/software platforms and infrastructure, and reasons for any limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS encourages making works produced with federal funds widely available, sharing work products via free and open-access journals and repositories when possible. Publications produced under an award should be made publicly accessible without charge. Identify delivery platforms, support for accessibility (e.g., via standard web browsers, IIIF), and any access restrictions with justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Access, licensing, and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify any licenses under which digital products will be shared (e.g., Creative Commons), describe what intellectual property rights will be asserted and any limitations, and address privacy concerns or cultural sensitivities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS expects applicants to release digital files under open-source licenses to maximize access and reuse. Work products resulting from IMLS funding should be distributed for free or at cost unless IMLS approves another arrangement. IMLS reserves a royalty-free, nonexclusive, irrevocable right to reproduce, publish, or otherwise use the work and authorize others to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Sustainability and preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe plans for preserving and maintaining digital products during and after the period of performance, identify appropriate retention lengths for different products, and address storage systems, shared repositories, technical documentation, migration planning, and organizational funding commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between products requiring permanent preservation versus those appropriate for medium- or short-term retention. Discuss preservation strategy, responsibilities, and long-term resource commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to FADGI resources
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS participates in the Federal Agencies Digital Guidelines Initiative (FADGI) and points applicants to FADGI for common standards, guidelines, methods, and best practices for creating digital collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FADGI provides links to relevant standards and recommendations; the list is not exhaustive and IMLS does not endorse specific resources. Applicants may consult FADGI for useful guidance and cite relevant standards in their Digital Products Plan.
